$comment: VAPP-33: steer over eNet's chat channel (`exp/enet/chat/1`, acked, ONE ordered stream per peer) between a viewer install and the install RUNNING the session. The steer frames themselves are unchanged (apps/steer-relay/src/protocol.ts + STEER-WIRE-EXP-850.md); only the carrier moves. ENVELOPE: one chat message = UTF-8 JSON `{t:"exp-steer", v:1, sessionId, frames:[...]}`, frames = wire frame OBJECTS (never strings), applied in array order, envelopes in chat order. `parse` rules (every receiver): t must be `exp-steer`, v must be 1, sessionId a non-empty string, frames a NON-EMPTY array of objects each with a string `t` (the wire frames' own tag, exactly the relay's `{t:"input",data}` etc.); anything else is not a steer envelope (ignored, acked). A frame whose `t` the receiver does not know is skipped, the rest of the envelope still applies. VIEWER → DEVICE frames: `join {channel:"activity"}`, `leave`, and the relay client frames `input`, `answer`, `interrupt`, `unqueue`, `set_config`, `set_mode`, `kill`, `history_page {requestId, beforeSeq, limit}` (its session is the envelope's). Frames go out exactly as on the relay socket (e.g. `{t:"join",channel:"activity"}`, `{t:"answer",questionId,keys,text?}`). DEVICE → VIEWER: on `join` = `activity_reset`, the journal replay (`activity {event, seq}` in `replay_seq` order: the log, then the latest-wins slots), then `activity_synced {firstSeq, lastSeq, truncated?}` (the end-of-replay marker, exactly the relay's: firstSeq/lastSeq = the seqs of the first and last LOG entry (the latest-wins slots do not count), both 0 when the log is empty; `truncated: true` when the journal evicted or firstSeq > 0, absent otherwise); afterwards every recorded event live as `activity {event, seq}`; `history_chunk {requestId, events, seqs, done}` to the asker only; `keepalive` every `keepaliveMs` to every joined viewer; `bye {outcome}` when the run ends (the viewer is dropped); `error {code}` with `no_such_session` (this install neither runs the session live nor holds its stored journal: the viewer tries its next endpoint) or `unauthorized` (the access rule). STORED REPLAY (VAPP-43, replaces the relay's `history_request` + lingering rooms): a `join` for a session this install does not run live but whose journal file it holds (EXP-773 `{data_dir}/journal/<sessionId>.jsonl`) is answered from the file under the same access rule, the audience (team, starter, shared) read off the device's synced `sessions` row (no row = `no_such_session`): `activity_reset`, the file's whole replay (`read_journal_seq`), `activity_synced` (`truncated` absent: nothing was evicted), then, for an ENDED row, `bye {outcome:"history"}` (the viewer is dropped); for a row still alive (idle: its run went away between turns) the viewer stays joined: `keepalive`s, `history_page` answered from the file, and once the run's publisher comes back on this install every such viewer is handed to it as a fresh join (`activity_reset` + full replay). A re-sent `join` restarts the feed (activity_reset + full replay), exactly like a relay reconnect. BATCHING (the device): a viewer's feed drains its queue into one envelope while the serialized envelope stays ≤ `batchMaxBytes`; a frame that alone passes it goes in an envelope of its own; an envelope over `chatMaxBytes` (enet-core MAX_CHAT_MESSAGE) is never sent (the frame is dropped and logged). A failed or timed-out (`sendTimeoutMs`) send drops the viewer. DISCOVERY: the viewer calls tRPC `installs.forSession {sessionId}` → `[{endpointId, kind}]` = the non-revoked `desktop`/`daemon` installs whose `device_id` = the session's `device_id`, newest `last_seen_at` first, only for a caller who can see the session (the visibility rule: starter, or `shared` + team member). It sends `join` to the first; on `error no_such_session` the next; no endpoint, no node, every endpoint refused, or no `activity_synced` within `joinTimeoutMs` = NO FEED: since VAPP-43 the steer relay carries no session content, so there is no fallback. The viewer shows its EXISTING states with their existing copy: a row still alive = `starting` ("The live stream isn't up yet. The desktop may still be connecting.") and redials on its backoff; an ended row = `ended` with the device-offline copy ("{device} is offline. The transcript lives on that machine."). A viewer that sees no frame for `staleMs` re-sends `join`. ACCESS (the device, per envelope): the sender endpoint's user comes from the registry list of the SESSION's team (`installs.list {teamId: sessions.team_id}` entries; an endpoint known only from another team the device's user shares with the sender does NOT count); unknown endpoint = refused; the starter (`sessions.user_id`) = allowed; another user = allowed only when the session is `shared` (being in that team's list = a member). `access` cases: {viewerUserId (null = endpoint not in the session team's registry list), starterUserId, shared} → allowed. VIEWER SIDE: device frames arrive as chat messages the DEVICE dials (each side sends on its own outbound stream, so the viewer's allowlist must hold the device's endpoint: the same team registry); the viewer applies only envelopes whose sessionId it joined AND whose sender is the endpoint it joined, every other steer envelope is ignored. `parse` cases: {body (the chat body as a JSON value, or bodyText for a raw string)} → {ok, sessionId?, types? (the frames' `t` tags kept, in order)}. `batch` cases: frame sizes in bytes (each frame's serialized JSON length) with the envelope overhead `overhead` (the serialized envelope with an empty frames array) and one comma per extra frame → the groups as frame indexes; `dropped` = indexes over chatMaxBytes even alone.

access.name: the starter of a shared session
an endpoint the registry does not know

parse.name: a composer message: text chunk then the submitting CR
an unknown frame type is kept by parse (the receiver skips it)

batch.name: split at the budget (overhead + sizes + commas)
a frame over the chat cap is dropped
